ops.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. EU AI ACT — DIGITAL OMNIBUS STATUS: The 7 May 2026 provisional agreement (Annex III postponed to 2 December 2027; Annex I to 2 August 2028; new Article 5 prohibition on AI-generated CSAM and non-consensual intimate imagery; watermarking compliance set at 2 December 2026) is now in legal-linguistic revision. Formal Council and Parliament endorsement must complete before 2 August 2026; if it slips, the original AI Act dates re-activate. AUSTRALIA: The first mandatory requirement under the Policy for the responsible use of AI in government begins 15 June 2026 — approximately four weeks away. The AI impact assessment tool and mandatory APS foundational AI training are the two binding mechanisms. Australia continues to rely on existing laws and sector regulators rather than a standalone AI Act for the broader economy. FUNDING: Carta Q1 2026 confirms AI startups now take ~50% of all pre-seed dollars and 33% of total VC funding. AI seed rounds carry a 42% valuation premium; median pre-money ~$17.9M. Seed deal count fell 31% year-on-year in Q1 even as total seed dollars rose ~30% — capital is concentrating into fewer, larger checks. SOLO FOUNDER: Solo-founded US startups have risen from 23.7% of new companies in 2019 to 36.3% by mid-2025. A solo founder's AI agent stack now runs $300–$500/month in subscriptions for what would be $80K–$120K/month in headcount. Microsoft Agent 365 went GA on 1 May 2026 at $15/user/month standalone (or bundled in the $99 E7 Frontier Worker Suite) — the first hyperscaler-grade agent governance plane. RISKS: Omnibus formal-adoption slip past 2 August 2026 remains the live tail risk; Australia's June 15 deadline is now close enough that any future government-sector positioning should already factor it in. OPPORTUNITIES: Annex III runway extension to December 2027 gives time to harden documentation; the solo-founder cost-arbitrage data underwrites SageReasoning's R&D phase economics.

ANTHROPIC: Opus 4.7 has been GA since 16 April 2026 at unchanged pricing ($5/$25 per million tokens), with a 13% improvement on Opus 4.6 on the 93-task coding benchmark and substantially better vision. Public references in Claude Code source code indicate the next Sonnet version will be 4.8 (skipping 4.7), expected within the May window. The advisor tool remains in beta. Anthropic's enterprise push is accelerating: ten ready-to-run financial-services agent templates and Microsoft 365 add-ins for Excel, PowerPoint, and Word shipped this period, with Claude now available in Microsoft Copilot mainline chat via the Frontier program. VERCEL — NEXT.JS MAY 2026 SECURITY RELEASE (7 May 2026): 13 advisories patched in 15.5.18 and 16.2.6; scope spans denial of service, middleware/proxy bypass, SSRF (CVE-2026-44578 via WebSocket-upgrade handling), cache poisoning, XSS, and an App Router segment-prefetch bypass that allows authenticated routes to leak to unauthenticated callers. NO patches are planned for 13.x or 14.x; upgrade is the only complete mitigation; WAF rules are not a reliable workaround. SUPABASE: Pricing unchanged — Free / $25 Pro / $599 Team / Enterprise; auth MAU pricing $0.00325 beyond plan caps. SECURITY — NEW CRITICAL CVEs THIS WEEK: Microsoft Patch Tuesday (12 May 2026) addressed 118 CVEs including CVE-2026-41089 (Windows Netlogon RCE, CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2026-41103 (Microsoft SSO plugin for Jira/Confluence elevation of privilege, CVSS 9.1). CVE-2026-42897 — an Exchange Server OWA XSS spoofing zero-day (CVSS 8.1) — was disclosed 14 May 2026 and is being exploited in the wild against on-premises Exchange 2016/2019/SE. CVE-2026-23918 is a double-free / possible RCE in Apache HTTP/2 (CVSS 8.8) fixed in 2.4.67. LLM COSTS: Prompt caching is now treated as standard practice at both Anthropic and OpenAI; production case studies report 40–80% savings, with semantic caching pushing FAQ hit rates above 80%. Model routing remains the highest-impact single lever. RISKS — FOUNDER ATTENTION: Patch Next.js immediately if not already done; verify hosted Exchange exposure if any; the Apache HTTP/2 fix matters for any self-hosted reverse-proxy path. OPPORTUNITIES: Caching-first prompt design and tiered model routing remain the cheapest cost-control levers heading into Stripe wiring (P4).

support.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. ACCESSIBILITY — SECTION 504 DEADLINE EXTENDED (7 May 2026): HHS Office for Civil Rights issued an Interim Final Rule extending the digital-accessibility compliance deadline under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. Recipients with 15+ employees now have until 11 May 2027; those with fewer than 15 employees until 10 May 2028. Last week's summary noted the original 11 May 2026 date arriving 'today' — that date no longer governs. The underlying standard is still WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA. OCR enforcement authority under the rule remains live (rule effective since 8 July 2024). MENTAL HEALTH AI — REGULATORY EXPANSION: Tennessee's law (signed 1 April 2026, effective 1 July 2026) prohibits AI systems presenting themselves as qualified mental health professionals. California's SB 243 (effective 1 January 2026) requires AI-disclosure, 3-hour break reminders for minors, and self-harm detection. New York continues to require suicidal-ideation detection, crisis-hotline referral, and non-human disclosure. Illinois and Nevada maintain full bans on AI for behavioural health. Q1 2026: 36 states introduced 70+ bills regulating AI chatbots — disclosure is the dominant clause. PUBLIC SENTIMENT — STANFORD 2026 AI INDEX: 76% of Americans trust AI rarely or only sometimes versus 21% trusting most/almost always. 50% feel more concerned than excited about increased AI use, with only 10% more excited. 41% say federal AI regulation won't go far enough. The Pew international comparison (25 countries) reports a median 53% trust the EU on AI governance versus 37% the US and 27% China. AI SAFETY: OECD's February 2026 paper on AI-incident trends (No. 53) tracks 14 thematic clusters across the OECD.AI Incidents Monitor (~14,901 incidents). The 362/2025 vs 233/2024 figure (2026 AI Index) and the 28%→18% organisational confidence drop in incident response remain the standing baseline. PHILOSOPHICAL COUNSELLING / WELLBEING: No material new developments this week. RISKS — FOUNDER ATTENTION: New York's specific requirements remain the de-facto template for R20a design; the Section 504 deadline shift means WCAG 2.1 AA is still the live standard but the compliance horizon for covered entities has loosened — competitor sites may slow their accessibility investment, which is more reason for SageReasoning to land WCAG 2.1 AA early as a differentiator. OPPORTUNITIES: The low public-trust environment continues to align with R18a honest-certification framing and R19 limitations-page commitments.
